brief.headline: Yesterday's three signs of a market finding a level all reversed in one session - the contango widened to its widest yet, the price fall re-accelerated and the warehouse draw stopped dead at zero - while the only genuinely strong number on the page came from Chinese buyers emptying warehouses ahead of a holiday.
bullets: WHAT MOVED, AND THE HONEST CORRECTION: on Thursday's LME official aluminium cash settled $3,228.00 and three-month $3,252.50. Cash fell $12.00, or 0.37%, which is SIX TIMES the previous session's $2.00. Yesterday this page made the shrinking size of each daily fall its headline and argued the market had almost stopped falling. One session later that is wrong, and it is corrected here rather than dropped. Cash has now fallen on six of the last seven settled sessions.

THE CURVE DID NOT FIND A LEVEL: the cash-to-three-month contango WIDENED to $24.50 from $20.00, the widest reading of this entire sequence. Five sessions ago the market paid a $21.00 premium for immediate metal; it now pays $24.50 to defer it. The $20.00 that looked like a floor for two rings was a pause inside a widening. A widening contango is the market saying it is easier to wait than to own, and it has now said so four times in five sessions.

THE WAREHOUSE DRAW STOPPED AT EXACTLY ZERO: visible LME stock was unchanged at 241,375 tonnes, the day after a 750-tonne draw this page had called a signal rather than a rounding. Three draws followed by a flat zero is not a trend. What does survive is the level: inventory remains near multi-decade lows and about 9,840 tonnes under the August average, so the structural tightness argument is untouched even though the day-to-day momentum argument is not.

WHAT TO WATCH, AND WHERE THE GOOD NEWS ACTUALLY IS: the strongest number on the page is Chinese. Public trade data show aluminium ingot inventory at major consumption sites down 118,000 tonnes across two weeks before the National Day holiday - 63,000 tonnes on 17-September and 55,000 on 24-September - described as the steepest fall for that period in the 2020-2026 record, with cast alloy stocks ending a six-week build. Against that, physical metal in South China still traded at repeated discounts on the same day, and the US ten-year Treasury yield pushed on to 5.142%. Watch today's 13:20 London official for whether the contango widens a fifth time.

lme.commentary: THE SESSION REVERSED THREE OF THE FOUR SIGNALS THIS PAGE LED WITH YESTERDAY, AND THAT IS THE CENTRAL FACT OF THIS RUN. Yesterday's page argued that the aluminium market was finding a level: the flat-price decline had almost stopped at $2.00, the contango had settled at $20.00 for two rings, and the warehouse draw had grown ten-fold to 750 tonnes. On the 24-September official all three of those turned. CASH FELL $12.00, SIX TIMES THE PREVIOUS SESSION'S FALL, to $3,228.00 - a fourth consecutive decline and a sixth in seven settled sessions. THE CONTANGO WIDENED $4.50 TO $24.50, the widest reading of the entire sequence, which now runs a $21.00 backwardation five sessions ago, then contangos of $10.50, $22.00, $20.00 and $24.50: the $20.00 was a pause inside a widening, not a floor. AND THE STOCK DRAW STOPPED AT EXACTLY ZERO, with visible inventory unchanged at 241,375 tonnes. This page downgraded its risk-register arrow on the contango row from UP to FLAT yesterday on the strength of a two-session pause; that arrow goes back to UP today, and the reversal is published as a reversal rather than applied quietly. THE ONE SIGNAL THAT DID NOT REVERSE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED LEAST FOR THE DAY AND MOST FOR THE YEAR: the level of inventory. At 241,375 tonnes stock remains near multi-decade lows and about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215. The structural scarcity argument rests on the level and is untouched; what has been damaged is the session-by-session momentum argument that had been built on top of it, and the two should not have been conflated. THREE-MONTH RESOLVED ITS PRE-REGISTERED TEST DOWNWARD. It settled $3,252.50, $8.50 below the 3,261 line this page had published as the consolidation-versus-break threshold, on a second consecutive close beneath it. Yesterday it closed one dollar below and this page refused to call that a break, on the grounds that a dollar is inside any reasonable definition of noise. Waiting was correct; waiting further would not be. The test is resolved and the resolution is bearish. Three-month's cushion over the August mean of $3,251.23 has shrunk from $8.77 to $1.27. THE VERIFICATION ON THIS BOARD IS THE STRONGEST OF THIS SEQUENCE AND IS WORTH STATING BECAUSE EARLIER RUNS IN THIS WINDOW WERE NOT SO LUCKY. The English and German Westmetall overviews were both re-requested cache-busted and agree to the cent across all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings - so the language-divergence failure recorded on 12-September, where German led and English lagged, is absent and cannot be masking a stale snapshot. The per-metal aluminium daily table has also rolled to 24-September and shows no row after it, so overview and table are aligned rather than one leading the other, which is the first fully aligned pair in this window. All five stock lines reconcile arithmetically against the levels carried yesterday. And a public macro reference board read at the same hour carries aluminium at $3,255.75, bracketing the official cash and three-month legs as a contract-for-difference mark should. THE CROSS-METAL READ IS BEING RETIRED. Today four of five fronts moved towards immediacy and aluminium alone moved away; yesterday it was the exact mirror; the day before, close to the mirror again. Copper's backwardation widened $77.00 to $125.00, zinc's widened $56.00 to $65.50, nickel's contango narrowed $170.00 to $155.00, lead's narrowed $42.50 to $25.00. A signal that flips sign three sessions running is noise in the front, not a regime, and this page will stop trying to read a market-wide carry story out of it. What survives is narrower and genuinely useful: ALUMINIUM HAS LOOSENED ITS FRONT ON FOUR OF THE LAST FIVE RINGS WHILE COPPER AND ZINC HAVE TIGHTENED THEIRS, so the aluminium front is behaving differently from its two closest comparables, and that relative divergence rather than the daily direction is the durable observation. One oddity is flagged without explanation because no public source offers one: zinc tightened its front while its inventory BUILT 8,325 tonnes, or 7.25%, the largest single stock move on this board in this window.

drivers.text: The exchange curve widened its contango to the widest of the sequence - the buyer argument strengthened, and yesterday's framing is withdrawn — On the 24-September LME official, cash settled $3,228.00 against three-month $3,252.50, a $24.50 CONTANGO WIDENED from $20.00 and the widest reading of this sequence. Yesterday this page argued the contango had found a level and that the buyer's argument had weakened accordingly; that was wrong and is corrected here. A market that pays $24.50 to DEFER metal rather than to own it now is a market in which a buyer can credibly refuse to pay a rising premium for prompt delivery - and the argument is stronger today than at any point in this sequence, because the curve has now loosened on four of the last five rings. The mechanism is not speculative: premiums are paid for immediacy, and immediacy is exactly what this curve says is cheap.
drivers.source: Westmetall - LME official prices (24-September-2026 session; EN and DE overviews cache-busted and in exact agreement)

drivers.text: Chinese pre-holiday destocking is the steepest on the 2020-2026 record, which is the strongest counter-argument on the page — SMM's published inventory statistics for 24-September record aluminium ingot inventory at major domestic consumption sites falling for two consecutive weeks before the National Day holiday - DOWN 63,000 TONNES ON 17-SEPTEMBER AND A FURTHER 55,000 TONNES ON 24-SEPTEMBER, 118,000 tonnes in two weeks - and SMM describes it explicitly as the steepest decline for the same period in previous years across its 2020-2026 comparison. On the same day SMM reported cast aluminium alloy ingot social inventory down 2,700 tonnes week on week to 31,800 tonnes, ENDING A SIX-WEEK BUILD. Physical metal leaving warehouses at a record pre-holiday pace is the strongest single argument against the soft-demand reading of the exchange curve. THE HONEST QUALIFIER IS THE TIMING: this is holiday stockpiling, it is seasonal, and SMM itself flags that whether demand sustains after the holiday still warrants attention. A stock draw driven by a calendar is not the same as a stock draw driven by consumption.
drivers.source: SMM - Aluminum inventory plummets before 2026 National Day, dropping 118,000 tonnes in two weeks (24-September-2026)

drivers.text: The Chinese physical market still cleared at repeated discounts on the very day inventory was falling fastest — SMM's 24-September South China spot review records that market participants initially held quotes firm but that, with month-end approaching and the need to cash out before the holiday dominant, QUOTES WERE LOWERED REPEATEDLY AND MOST TRANSACTIONS WERE CONCLUDED AT ACTUAL DISCOUNTS, with spot circulation shifting to oversupply and overall trading activity weak. SMM records phased downstream stockpiling as essentially complete and the procurement pace slowing. THIS SITS DIRECTLY AGAINST THE DESTOCKING HEADLINE AND BOTH ARE FROM THE SAME SOURCE ON THE SAME DAY, so this page publishes the tension rather than picking the convenient half: inventory is leaving warehouses fast, and sellers are still having to cut price to move it. The most defensible reading is that the draw is being bought at the buyer's price, not the seller's.
drivers.source: SMM - Aluminum prices edged down today, spot market weakened; South China aluminum spot daily review (24-September-2026)

drivers.text: US regional pricing remains set by policy arithmetic, and the arithmetic moved today only because the metal price did — The Section 232 headline rate is re-verified and unchanged at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. At the 24-September cash settlement of $3,228.00 the 50% rate alone is worth $1,614.00 a tonne, DOWN $6.00 from yesterday's $1,614-equivalent purely as a function of the lower exchange price - the policy did not move, the multiplicand did. logistics.note: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 23-SEPTEMBER-2026. THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL NEW PUBLIC INFORMATION THIS RUN IS DIPLOMATIC RATHER THAN OPERATIONAL, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. SMM's 23-September summary records that on 22-September US President Trump, speaking at the 81st UN General Assembly, reiterated that the United States would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER THE NOVEMBER MIDTERM ELECTIONS; that Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met US envoy Witkoff in New York and Trump described a three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation as very productive with another to be arranged; and that Iran has publicly set CONDITIONS for reopening the Strait of Hormuz - immediate lifting of the maritime blockade, immediate unfreezing of all Iranian assets, and an end to the war on all regional fronts. READ THIS CAREFULLY RATHER THAN OPTIMISTICALLY. A negotiation is now visibly under way, which is the first genuine de-escalation signal of this cycle. But the publicly stated US timetable puts any agreement AFTER November, and Iran's stated conditions are maximalist. The transit constraint is therefore still in force today and is not publicly guided to clear inside this quarter. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT AS SETTLED OUTCOMES. WHY THE ARROW IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT AND NOT TO DOWN: the direction of news has genuinely changed - talks are happening, are described by one party as productive, and a reopening condition set has been publicly articulated, which is more than existed at any point in this cycle. But NOTHING OPERATIONAL HAS CHANGED. headlines.title: THE CONTANGO WIDENED TO $24.50, THE WIDEST OF THIS SEQUENCE, AND YESTERDAY'S 'FOUND A LEVEL' READ IS WITHDRAWN. Cash settled $3,228.00 against three-month $3,252.50 on the 24-September official. The five-session sequence now reads a $21.00 BACKWARDATION, then contangos of $10.50, $22.00, $20.00 and $24.50 - so the $20.00 that held for two rings was a pause inside a widening, not a floor. This page downgraded its risk-register arrow on this row from UP to FLAT yesterday on the strength of that pause; the arrow goes back to UP today and the reversal is stated rather than quietly applied. A market paying to defer metal is the opposite of a market short of it.

THE DECLINE RE-ACCELERATED SIX-FOLD AND THE DECELERATION STORY IS BROKEN. Cash fell $12.00 or 0.37% after falls of $22.50, $20.50 and $2.00 on the three preceding sessions. Yesterday this page led with the shrinking size of each fall and argued the market had almost stopped going down; one session later that reading is wrong and it is corrected here rather than dropped. Cash has now fallen on six of the last seven settled sessions and sits $21.63 below the August monthly mean of $3,249.63 and $62.00 below the September-to-date mean of $3,290.00.

THE 3,261 TEST RESOLVED DOWNWARD ON A SECOND CLOSE BENEATH IT. Three-month settled $3,252.50, $8.50 below the level this page pre-registered as the consolidation-versus-break line, after closing one dollar below it yesterday. This page refused to call a one-dollar margin a break and was right to wait; an $8.50 margin held across two sessions is the test resolving, and this page calls it now rather than waiting further. Three-month's cushion over the August mean has shrunk from $8.77 to $1.27.

THE STOCK DRAW STOPPED AT EXACTLY ZERO, ONE SESSION AFTER THIS PAGE CALLED IT A SIGNAL. Visible LME aluminium stock was unchanged at 241,375 tonnes - a reported change of zero - ending a three-session draw run the day after its largest draw at 750 tonnes. Three draws followed by a flat zero is not a trend, and that is recorded against this page's own framing. WHAT SURVIVES IS THE LEVEL RATHER THAN THE MOMENTUM: inventory remains near multi-decade lows and about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215, so the structural scarcity argument is untouched while the day-to-day one is not.

CHINESE PRE-HOLIDAY DESTOCKING IS THE STEEPEST ON SMM'S 2020-2026 RECORD AND IS THE STRONGEST NUMBER ON THIS PAGE TODAY. SMM's published inventory statistics for 24-September record aluminium ingot inventory at major domestic consumption sites down 63,000 tonnes on 17-September and a further 55,000 tonnes on 24-September - 118,000 TONNES IN TWO WEEKS - and SMM describes it explicitly as the steepest decline for the same period in previous years. Physical metal leaving warehouses at a record pre-holiday pace is a genuine demand signal. THE QUALIFIER IS SEASONALITY: this is holiday stockpiling, and SMM itself flags that whether demand sustains after the holiday warrants attention.

METAL CLEARED AT REPEATED DISCOUNTS ON THE VERY DAY INVENTORY FELL FASTEST, AND BOTH FACTS COME FROM THE SAME SOURCE. SMM's 24-September South China spot review records participants initially holding quotes firm, then lowering them repeatedly as the month-end need to cash out before the holiday dominated, with most transactions concluded at actual discounts, spot circulation shifting to oversupply and trading activity weak. Phased downstream stockpiling is described as essentially complete and the procurement pace as slowing. The most defensible reading is that the record draw is being bought at the buyer's price, not the seller's.

THE ALUMINA PANEL GOT ITS FIRST REFRESH IN A MONTH AND IT PRINTED ALMOST EXACTLY FLAT. SMM's weekly alumina index for 24-September stands at 2,671.59 yuan/tonne, down 2.35 yuan/tonne or 0.09% week on week, with ALL FIVE REGIONAL QUOTES UNCHANGED week on week - Shandong 2,640-2,710, Henan 2,680-2,740, Shanxi 2,670-2,730, Guangxi 2,580-2,630, Guizhou 2,720-2,780. A flat index built from five flat regions is a genuinely quiet market rather than an average hiding offsetting moves. This replaces a 25-August mark of 2,600 yuan/tonne that this page had been carrying for a month, and the gap between the two is a month of drift, not a session's move.

CHINESE ALUMINA SUPPLY ROSE INTO A FLAT PRICE, WHICH IS SUPPORTIVE FOR SMELTER MARGINS. SMM reports China's national weekly alumina operating rate UP 0.23 percentage points to 76.89% as of 24-September, on total installed metallurgical-grade capacity of 119.62 million tonnes a year and operating capacity of 91.97 million tonnes a year. By region Shandong held at 89.20%, Shanxi at 72.48%, Henan at 59.83%, Guizhou at 81.33%, with only Guangxi easing 0.21 points to 79.45%. Alumina is roughly a third of a smelter's cash cost and it takes about two tonnes to make one tonne of metal, so more alumina at an unmoved price widens the smelting margin.

THE ENERGY COST FLOOR ROSE FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE SESSION AND THIS TIME HARD. Brent rose about 3.90% to $107.10 on the 24-September reference session after 2.41% the day before, comfortably reclaiming the $100 handle after a five-session losing streak, with WTI up 3.74% to $95.61 and European gas TTF up 3.71% to EUR 74.68. Energy is the single largest line in a smelter's cash cost, so this raises the floor under the marginal tonne. It is one of the few unambiguously supportive readings on the page and it cuts directly against the softening flat price.

THE US TEN-YEAR TREASURY YIELD PUSHED ON TO 5.142%, ADDING ABOUT SEVEN BASIS POINTS TO YESTERDAY'S NINETEEN-YEAR HIGH, AND THE DOLLAR ROSE A SECOND DAY. The dollar index gained 0.20% to 101.293 and the LME euro fixing fell 0.38% to 1.13690. A higher financing cost pushes forward curves towards contango and aluminium's contango did widen - CONSISTENT. But this page stays careful: on the identical ring copper's and zinc's fronts TIGHTENED rather than loosened, so a single financing cost cannot be driving all five fronts. Rates are a contributing pressure on aluminium's curve, not a complete explanation of it.

THE CROSS-METAL FRONT SIGNAL REVERSED ITS SIGN FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION, AND THIS PAGE IS RETIRING IT AS A READ. Today copper's backwardation widened $77.00 to $125.00, zinc's widened $56.00 to $65.50, nickel's contango narrowed $170.00 to $155.00 and lead's narrowed $42.50 to $25.00 - four of five fronts moving TOWARDS immediacy - while aluminium alone moved away. That is the mirror of yesterday and close to the mirror of the day before. A signal that flips sign three sessions running is noise. WHAT SURVIVES IS NARROWER AND MORE USEFUL: aluminium has loosened its front on four of the last five rings while copper and zinc have tightened theirs, so the relative divergence, not the daily direction, is the durable observation.

ZINC POSTED THE LARGEST STOCK MOVE ON THE BOARD AND TIGHTENED ITS FRONT AT THE SAME TIME. Zinc inventory BUILT 8,325 tonnes, or 7.25%, to 123,200 from 114,875 - by far the biggest single-session stock move of any metal in this window - while zinc's backwardation WIDENED from $56.00 to $65.50. A front tightening while inventory jumps more than seven per cent in a session is internally odd, and it means either the build did not land where the tightness is or the tightness is not about visible stock. This page has no publicly sourced explanation for it and will not invent one; it is flagged because it is a reminder that visible inventory and front-end tightness are not the same variable.

CAST ALUMINIUM ALLOY INGOT INVENTORY ENDED A SIX-WEEK BUILD, FALLING 2,700 TONNES WEEK ON WEEK TO 31,800 TONNES. SMM attributes the shift to a widening spot-futures price spread and the release of pre-holiday stockpiling demand, with enterprises showing improved purchasing appetite, and expects further destocking as the National Day holiday arrives. The same note flags explicitly that whether demand can be sustained AFTER the holiday still warrants attention. Ending a six-week build is a real turn; doing it on holiday stocking is a qualified one.

DOWNSTREAM OPERATING RATES WERE STABLE RATHER THAN STRONG. SMM's weekly downstream survey records the operating rate of leading Chinese aluminium processing enterprises at 62.1%, UP JUST 0.2 PERCENTAGE POINTS WEEK ON WEEK, with pre-holiday stockpiling progressing in an orderly manner and operating rates across all sectors generally stable. A 0.2-point move is within any reasonable definition of flat. It is a useful corrective to the destocking headline: metal is leaving warehouses far faster than processors are increasing the rate at which they consume it, which is what stockpiling rather than consumption looks like.

THE SECTION 232 RATE IS RE-VERIFIED AND UNCHANGED AT 50% ON ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. At the 24-September cash settlement of $3,228.00 the 50% rate is worth $1,614.00 a tonne on its own, DOWN $6.00 on the day purely because the exchange price fell - the policy did not move, the multiplicand did. Against a US Midwest duty-paid row of $2,403/t that is roughly two-thirds of the delivered US regional premium. Anyone reading the US premium as a scarcity signal is reading a tax rate. The EU comparison is a 6% duty, about $194/t on the same cash price.

THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.note: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL, AND IT CARRIES THE WEEKLY CLOSE - THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE SCHEDULED ITEM ON THIS PAGE. Two things resolve at 13:20 London. FIRST, whether the contango widens a FIFTH time in six rings after reaching $24.50, the widest of this sequence: a further widening turns a sequence into a trend and this page would treat it as one; a narrowing back inside $20.00 would make today's widening the outlier rather than yesterday's pause. SECOND, and larger, today is FRIDAY, so this official sets the WEEKLY CLOSE against the 3,261 level that the weekly Elliott count turns on. Three-month has closed below 3,261 on two consecutive daily officials but has NOT yet produced a weekly close beneath it. A weekly close below 3,261 is the published condition for shifting weight materially towards the weekly alternate count; a weekly close above it leaves the constructive count intact for another week.

THE 3,261 TEST RESOLVED DOWNWARD ON THE DAILY TIMEFRAME AND IS NOW CLOSED. Three-month settled $3,252.50, $8.50 below the level, on a second consecutive close beneath it after closing one dollar below on 23-September. This page refused to call a one-dollar margin a break and waited; an $8.50 margin held across two sessions is the test resolving, and this page calls it now rather than waiting further. The daily-degree alternate count is raised accordingly. NOTE WHAT IS NOT YET RESOLVED: the WEEKLY close, which prints today and is a separate and higher-degree test.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING, AND ITS RELEVANCE IS NOW THE HIGHEST IT HAS BEEN ON THIS PAGE. The US ten-year printed a NINETEEN-YEAR HIGH of 5.073% on 23-September and US flash September PMIs hit multi-year highs - manufacturing 57, services 58.7, composite 58.4 - with SMM reporting expectations for an October increase INTENSIFYING and Governor Barr saying further increases may be needed. With the dot plot at a 4.1% median for 2026 and two meetings left, the projections imply at least one further rise before year-end. Carry acts on the CURVE rather than the flat price, and the curve is where this page's central question sits: a further increase argues against the contango reversing; a HOLD would remove the cleanest structural argument against a return to backwardation. THE QUALIFICATION THAT SURVIVES: copper widened its backwardation into this same cost on this same session.

THE NEXT DATED STEP IN THE US-CANADA TARIFF SCHEDULE, NOW FIVE DAYS OUT: a US vehicle and dairy import ban takes effect, following Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn in force since 08-September and the 08-September White House annex that lifted previously exempt downstream aluminium lines to a combined levy of up to 100%. THE CONTEXT THAT MAKES THIS DATE INTERESTING IS UNCHANGED AND UNRETRACTED: on 22-September Novelis was reported cutting production and about 80 jobs at Kingston, Ontario explicitly on Section 232 costs - the first clearly attributed capacity consequence of this cycle, arriving a week before the next escalation. At the 23-September cash settlement of $3,240.00 the 50% leg alone is about $1,620.00/t.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT - STILL THE LARGEST SINGLE DATED EVENT LEFT ON THIS PAGE AND NOW INSIDE TWO WEEKS. The pending range carried here is $280-310/t against a settled Q3 record of $395/t, a fall of 22-29% if it lands inside; it is unchanged for a NINTH consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. THE BUYER'S CASE STOPPED STRENGTHENING THIS RUN AND THIS PAGE SAYS SO: the exchange curve narrowed its contango $2.00 to $20.00 rather than deepening further, and the cross-metal pattern that reinforced the argument yesterday inverted. Alongside it sit producer offers of $310-325/t, Alba corroborated a FOURTH time at about 1.3 Mt, softer European premiums, and a central-China spot market transacting at a 50-80 yuan/mt discount to the October contract.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY REBUILD TEST - NOW THE CLEANEST FORWARD EXPERIMENT AVAILABLE ON CHINESE DEMAND, AND THIS RUN SHARPENED IT. Ingot inventory at major consumption sites fell 118,000 tonnes across the two weeks into the holiday, the steepest pre-holiday draw in SMM's 2020-2026 comparison, and cast alloy stocks ended a six-week build. SMM separately reports that China's aluminium industry is expected to MAINTAIN HIGH PRODUCTION through the holiday, so supply does not pause while demand takes a week off. THE EXPERIMENT: if the draw was genuine consumption, the post-holiday rebuild is shallow; if it was stockpiling - which the flat 62.1% processing operating rate and the discounted South China transactions both suggest - the rebuild is sharp and fast. SMM itself flags concentrated-arrival risk after the holiday. This page has no basis for pre-judging it and will report the rebuild when it prints.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE IS OPEN, OVERDUE AND HAS STILL NOT PRINTED - A SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN. Prebaked anode, coal tar pitch and green petcoke marks normally settle around the 17th-18th of each month. Nothing has published, so roughly a fifth of the smelter cash-cost stack is carried on marks about a month old. THE DIRECTIONAL SIGNPOST REVERSED THIS RUN AND THAT IS THE NEWS: Brent SNAPPED a five-session losing streak, rising 2.41% back above $101, and European gas rose about 1.34%. The case for a sharply LOWER settlement is now the weakest it has been this week. This page will append a mark to the input histories only when a dated public figure exists.

THE US-IRAN NEGOTIATING TRACK REMAINS PUBLIC, DATED AND UNCHANGED IN THE LAST 48 HOURS - AND IT IS STILL THE SINGLE LARGEST POTENTIAL SUPPLY-SIDE REPRICING ON THE PAGE. Trump reiterated on 22-September at the UN General Assembly that the US would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER the November midterm elections; Araghchi met Witkoff in New York, with a three-hour meeting described as very productive and another to be arranged; Iran publicly set conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz - lifting the maritime blockade, unfreezing all Iranian assets, ending the war on all regional fronts. THE TIMETABLE IS WHY THIS IS NOT PRICED AS IMMINENT: a post-November US timetable places any agreement outside this quarter, and Iran's conditions are maximalist. Nothing operational has changed on the water, and Brent's 2.41% rise on 23-September was publicly attributed to geopolitical RISK rather than relief.

THE CHINA-US TRADE TRACK REMAINS LIVE AND ITS RELEVANCE HERE IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN GENERAL. SMM's 24-September minutes record that the Chinese and US heads of state MET and that economic and trade lead persons held consultations in New York, with expectations of easing relations rising; groundwork was laid on 20-September when Vice Premier He Lifeng met Treasury Secretary Bessent and Trade Representative Greer. FOR THIS MARKET: regional delivered prices are currently set by tariff policy rather than physical scarcity, so any movement on the trade file transmits directly into the premium complex. Market commentary already attributes part of aluminium's recent support to expectations of easing, which makes DISAPPOINTMENT a live risk in the same window. The meeting happening is not the same as an outcome being published.

THE Q3-2026 PEER REPORTING SEASON OPENS AND ENDS THE CURRENT LULL. No peer result has been reported in the last 48 hours and the most recent on this page remains Constellium's Q2 of 29-July-2026, so the earnings panel is a historical record rather than a live one. The season opens with Alcoa in mid-October and runs through the Gulf, Indian and Chinese producers into November. It matters here because Q3 is the first full quarter priced against the post-June price collapse and the first in which the Gulf disruption, the restart pipeline and the Section 232 cost pass-through all appear together in reported segment numbers. No company's earnings history was back-filled this run because no exact publicly verified figure was obtained in this window.

risks.text: THE CONTANGO WIDENED TO THE WIDEST OF THE SEQUENCE AND THE TREND GOES BACK FROM FLAT TO UP AFTER ONE SESSION - THE DOWNGRADE PUBLISHED YESTERDAY IS REVERSED AND THE REVERSAL IS STATED RATHER THAN APPLIED QUIETLY. The cash-to-three-month spread widened $4.50 to a $24.50 CONTANGO on the 24-September official, the widest of this sequence, which now reads a $21.00 backwardation five sessions ago then contangos of $10.50, $22.00, $20.00 and $24.50. Two rings at $20.00 looked like a floor and were a pause. A widening contango is the exchange saying it is cheaper to wait than to own, and it is the single most consequential bearish signal on this page because it feeds directly into every premium and term negotiation. The published reversal condition is a return to backwardation and it remains unmet.

THE FEDERAL RESERVE PATH AND THE FINANCING COST ARE HELD AT UP AND THE EVIDENCE STRENGTHENED AGAIN. The US ten-year Treasury yield printed 5.142% on the 24-September reference session, adding about seven basis points to the 5.073% nineteen-year high carried yesterday, while the dollar index rose 0.20% to 101.293 and the LME euro fixing fell 0.38% to 1.13690 - a second consecutive session of dollar strength. Higher financing costs push forward curves towards contango and make dollar-priced metal dearer for non-dollar buyers. THE CAREFUL QUALIFIER THIS PAGE KEEPS ATTACHING: on the identical ring copper's and zinc's fronts tightened rather than loosened, so a single financing cost cannot be driving all five fronts and this channel is a contributing pressure on aluminium's curve, not a complete explanation.

TARIFF POLICY REMAINS THE DOMINANT SETTER OF REGIONAL PRICE AND THE TREND IS HELD AT FLAT - NO NEW INSTRUMENT AND NO NEW ATTRIBUTED CONSEQUENCE PRINTED INTO THIS WINDOW. The Section 232 headline rate is re-verified and unchanged at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. At the 24-September cash settlement of $3,228.00 the 50% rate is worth $1,614.00 a tonne on its own, down $6.00 on the day purely because the exchange price fell. Against a US Midwest duty-paid row of $2,403/t that is roughly two-thirds of the delivered premium, so the US regional number is predominantly a tax rather than a scarcity signal. The trend stays FLAT because the rate did not move; only the multiplicand did.

THE STOCK DRAWDOWN STOPPED AT EXACTLY ZERO AND THE TREND IS CUT FROM DOWN TO FLAT - THIS PAGE CALLED THE 750-TONNE DRAW A SIGNAL YESTERDAY AND A FLAT ZERO THE NEXT SESSION IS THE PLAINEST EVIDENCE AGAINST THAT. Visible LME stock was unchanged at exactly 241,375 tonnes on the 24-September ring, a reported change of zero, after draws of 75, 400 and 750 tonnes on the three preceding sessions. Three draws followed by a flat zero is not a trend and this page records that against its own framing of yesterday. WHAT SURVIVES IS THE LEVEL, NOT THE MOMENTUM: inventory remains near multi-decade lows and about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215, so the structural scarcity case is untouched. The arrow describes the direction of travel and the direction of travel has stopped.

THE GULF SUPPLY PICTURE REMAINS CONTESTED IN PUBLIC AND THE TREND IS HELD AT DOWN, WITH NO FIFTH CORROBORATION PRINTED AND THIS PAGE DECLINING TO COUNT RE-CITATIONS AS FRESH EVIDENCE. The operative public figure remains Aluminium Bahrain's operating capacity recovered to around 1.3 million tonnes, recorded in SMM's 24-September minutes citing foreign media reports. No fifth corroboration printed into this window, and this page stops counting at four: repeating the same underlying report through successive secondary citations does not make it more true. Set against that, a public market-news board updated 23-September records GCC production down 44% year on year in July against a region that supplied roughly 10% of global output before the war. The arrow stays DOWN because recovering ex-China capacity is bearish for price and the recovery is documented; what is missing is a primary company disclosure.

THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM OVERHANG IS HELD AT UP AND THE EVIDENCE GOT SHARPER AND MORE UNCOMFORTABLE. SMM's 24-September South China spot review records participants lowering quotes repeatedly, MOST TRANSACTIONS CONCLUDED AT ACTUAL DISCOUNTS, spot circulation shifting to oversupply, trading activity weak, phased downstream stockpiling essentially complete and the procurement pace slowing. On the same day SMM's weekly downstream survey put the processing operating rate at 62.1%, UP JUST 0.2 PERCENTAGE POINTS. The uncomfortable juxtaposition is that this sits alongside the steepest pre-holiday inventory draw in SMM's 2020-2026 record: metal is leaving warehouses far faster than processors are raising the rate at which they consume it, which is the signature of stockpiling rather than of consumption.

THE COST FLOOR IS HELD AT UP AND THE EVIDENCE DOUBLED. Brent rose about 3.90% to $107.10 on the 24-September reference session after 2.41% the day before - two strong up-sessions following a five-session losing streak, with the $100 handle comfortably reclaimed, WTI up 3.74% to $95.61 and European gas TTF up 3.71% to EUR 72.87-to-74.68. Energy is the single largest line in a smelter's cash cost, so the floor under the marginal tonne is rising while the metal price falls - a margin squeeze on the marginal producer and, at the extreme, the mechanism by which supply eventually leaves the market.
